items.q: What sort of content should I submit?
items.a:
Anything made while doing research or while observing a scientific subject. That could be imagery from microscopes, telescopes or high-speed cameras; visualizations of data, simulations or mathematical structures; or illustrations and interpretations of natural phenomena.

If you think it sits somewhere between science and art, send it in.

items.q: What if my entry is not from a formal lab or research project?
items.a: That's fine. Work inspired by science, made at home, in the field or in a studio is welcome, as long as there is a clear connection to a scientific idea, process or observation. Tell us about that connection in your description.

items.q: How recent should my work be?
items.a: We prefer work created within the last few years, but older pieces that have never been exhibited are also considered.

items.q: What sort of media do you accept?
items.a: Still images, videos and animations. Physical objects and installations are not accepted at this time.

items.q: Can I submit more than one image, animation or video?
items.a: Yes. You may submit up to three works. Please submit each one separately through the submission form.

items.q: How much does it cost to submit?
items.a: Nothing — submitting is free.

items.q: Who is eligible to participate?
items.a: Students, researchers, staff, faculty and members of our community. Describe your connection in the submission form.

items.q: What about alumni? Am I eligible to submit?
items.a: Yes, alumni are welcome to submit work.

items.q: What file format do you accept for images?
items.a: JPG, PNG or TIFF. Please do not compress or watermark the image.

items.q: What size or resolution should my image be?
items.a: As large as you have — ideally at least 3000 pixels on the longest side, so it can be printed at exhibition size.

items.q: What if my image comes from an instrument that only produces low resolution?
items.a: Submit it anyway and mention the instrument in your description. Our team will tell you if it can be printed at a suitable size.

items.q: Do you accept GIFs?
items.a: Animated GIFs should be submitted as videos (MP4). Still GIFs are accepted as images.

items.q: Where will accepted images be exhibited?
items.a: Accepted images are printed and shown in the physical exhibition, and also appear in the online gallery on this website.

items.q: How should I submit a video?
items.a: Upload it to YouTube, Vimeo or Google Drive and paste the link into the submission form. Make sure the link can be viewed by anyone who has it.

items.q: What is the maximum length of a video?
items.a: Three minutes. Shorter pieces usually work best in an exhibition space.

items.q: What video quality, resolution or frame rate should I use?
items.a: At least 1080p (1920×1080). Any standard frame rate (24, 25, 30 or 60 fps) is fine.

items.q: Can I submit VR or 360° videos?
items.a: Not at the moment — we can only show standard flat videos.

items.q: Where and how will accepted videos be exhibited?
items.a: Videos play on a loop on screens in the exhibition space, and are embedded in the online gallery.

items.q: What if my video has audio?
items.a: Videos are usually shown without sound in the gallery, so make sure your piece still works on mute. Audio will play in the online gallery.

items.q: What if I have a question that is not answered here?
items.a: Email us at the address on the Contact page and we'll get back to you.
